messages:
maya: FYI hitting repeated CUDA OOMs on serving-prod-7 despite headroom showing ~700-900MiB free. Alerts started ~03:46 UTC. Pods are restarting and paging is spiking. Suspect allocator/reserve mismatch + KV-cache churn.

infra-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: cuda-oom-ghost-reserve on cluster-prod at 2026-03-15T03:46:39Z · paging severity: high · assigned: oncall-nyc

thomas: seeing same. node=gpu-node-13 has 4 pods, two failed with container exits code OOM_KILLED. dmesg shows CUDA OOM+page faults. Attaching quick logs: 
```
[ 12345.678901] Out of memory: Killed process 4123 (serving-runtime) total-vm:13500000kB, anon-rss:4200000kB, file-rss:200kB, shmem-rss:0kB
[ 12345.679012] NVRM: GPU 0000:03:00.0: Xid (PCI:0000:03:00): 64, pid=4123, gpu context: 0x5a7b3
```

eli: headroom metric from allocator shows ~800MiB but nvtop & nvidia-smi show free 1.8GiB. That mismatch smells like reserved blocks held by stale CUDA contexts or the spare pool not being reclaimed. Also saw repeated small allocations and frees before crash -> fragmentation.

sarah: also seeing rapid increase in page-in/out on node: 
```
pgfaults: 24000 -> 48000 in 3m
writeback: 300MB -> 1.2GB
```

maya: customer impact: 3 customers on dedicated pools reported elevated latency and a small % of 5xx on gen endpoints. No full-service outage but degraded tails. Putting this as P2.

thomas: immediate mitigations I'm trying: 1) drain new requests from gpu-node-13 2) kill/restart offending containers to force full CUDA context teardown 3) reduce per-instance max_tokens to 512 on canary route 4) flip fallback to CPU for heavy tails

thomas: executed: `kubectl cordon gpu-node-13` and `kubectl rollout restart deploy/serving-runtime -l node=gpu-node-13 --timeout=60s` for the crashing replica set. Pods come back but one died again after ~90s.

eli: running a quick heap of GPU allocations via `nvidia-smi topo -m` and `pmap` on PID before kill; found ghost allocations pinned by resident processes in container runtime proxy. Suspect the daemon that manages KV cache (kv-cache-proxy) didn't free reserved_blocks on context loss.

maya: can you paste the allocator debug output? we have verbose allocator logging enabled on these nodes.

eli: allocator log snippet: 
```
[allocator] reserved_blocks_total=128 reserved_blocks_free=12 headroom_bytes=786432000 cache_reserved=5 pinned_reservations=7
[allocator] fragment_map: runs=943 holes=121 largest_hole=64MB avg_free_run=8MB
[allocator] reclaim_scan: freed_from_kv_cache=0 freed_from_sparepool=0 pinned_contexts=2
```

sarah: that matches — headroom_bytes is high but reserved_blocks_free low and pinned_reservations >0. reclaim_scan isn't able to free KV cache because contexts still show as active -> probably context leakage.

thomas: immediate workaround: disable KV cache on that deployment (set `KV_CACHE_MAX_BYTES=0`) and force a rolling restart. This should reduce pinned reservations and make allocator reclaimable. Doing that now on canary.

maya: do we have quick tradeoffs? Disabling KV cache will increase token cost and latency for cold prefixes. Customers on dedicated have SLAs; need to notify impacted teams.

infra-bot: ACTION: set env KV_CACHE_MAX_BYTES=0 on deployment/serving-prod-canary by thomas at 2026-03-15T04:02:10Z

eli: after restart, observed reserved_blocks_free jump from 12 -> 78 and headroom report stayed ~700MiB but actual free as seen by nvidia-smi increased. No OOM for 7m now on that node.

thomas: however one node still flapped: gpu-node-11 had a different failure mode — kernel driver reset showing Xid 79. That one likely hardware/driver. Filed hw ticket + moved workloads off node-11.

maya: routing policy update: switching model routing to prefer region fallback and reduce batch sizes for routing policy id=low-latency until stability confirmed. Pushed config at 04:18 UTC.

eli: further root cause hypothesis: allocator's sparepool has reserved slab segments sized for previous large-request patterns. When KV cache refuses to release on context loss, the pinned contexts hold slab fragments causing fragmentation; allocator still reports headroom because it counts total free but can't coalesce small holes to satisfy large contiguous allocations. Combined with paging pressure (host page cache busy) leads to OOM at allocation time.

thomas: long-term fixes proposed: 1) ensure kv-cache proxy acknowledges context teardown and forcibly frees reserved_blocks on container exit 2) add reclamation that coalesces small free runs (defrag pass) during high fragmentation 3) add early-detection alert for headroom/reserve divergence 4) add a graceful fallback to CPU on allocation failure instead of immediate container crash 5) improve operator runbook for draining + disabling KV cache.

maya: agreed. I'll open follow-up tickets after this call. For now, status: impacted nodes isolated, KV cache disabled on canary and then rollout to remaining pools starting with least-loaded. Customer 42 and Customer 77 saw transient 5xx; CS notified.

oncall-nyc: handoff note — I'm taking over the incident for the next 4 hours. Current mitigations: drained gpu-node-13, kv-cache disabled on canary, routing policy lowered batches, hardware ticket for node-11. Next steps: monitor for 30m windows of stability, then roll canary KV change to dedicated pools sequentially. If OOMs reappear, escalate to eng-runtime.

thomas: monitoring shows tail 99.9 latency improved after kv-cache disable by ~120ms and 5xx rate dropped to baseline. Keeping this thread open for 6h for postmortem notes. :thumbsup:

maya: filing incident postmortem draft now and tagging eng-runtime + eng-ml for allocator design review. Will include logs, allocator dumps, timeline, and suggested mitigations.

infra-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation applied; severity downgraded -> P2 at 2026-03-15T04:35:12Z.

sarah: small note — we should also instrument per-context reservation counts in metrics (prometheus) as `allocator_context_pinned_reservations` to make divergence visible earlier.

maya: agreed. Added to follow-ups. Thanks everyone for fast response.

oncall-nyc: closing note: I'm leaving a runbook step to 'if headroom>500MiB and reserved_free<20 -> disable KV cache on node group and restart runtime' until defrag/reclaim fixes are in.

thomas: acknowledged. I'll write the runbook update and link it to the postmortem.

maya: signing off incident channel, moving to postmortem drafting.
